'''Semur''' ({{IPA|id|səˈmʊr}}) is an Indonesian [[meat]] [[stew]] (mainly [[beef]]) [[braised]] in thick brown [[gravy]]. It is commonly found in [[Indonesian cuisine]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.thejakartapost.com/life/2018/04/30/indonesian-flavors-spice-up-moscow.html|title=Indonesian flavors spice up Moscow|work=The Jakarta Post|access-date=2018-05-11|language=en}}</ref> The main ingredients in the gravy are [[sweet soy sauce]], [[shallot]]s, [[onion]]s, [[garlic]], [[ginger]], [[candlenut]], [[nutmeg]], and [[cloves]] (and sometimes with [[black pepper]], [[coriander]], [[cumin]], and [[cinnamon]]).<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zMK9YIstmqoC&q=semur+indonesian+beef+stew&pg=PA81|title=27 Resep Hidangan Nasi Khas Indonesia not Only Nasi Goreng|last=Ganie|first=Suryatini N.|date=2009|publisher=Gramedia Pustaka Utama|isbn=9789792244519|language=id}}</ref>

[[Sweet soy sauce]] and candlenuts are the most important ingredients in the ''semur''-making process because they serve to strengthen the flavor, yet they must be blended harmoniously with the other ingredients. In addition to the spices and seasonings, ''semur'' also consists of a wide range of main ingredients with variation in presentation, such as meat (mainly [[beef]]), [[beef tongue]],<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rstGDwAAQBAJ&q=semur+indonesian+beef+stew&pg=PA66|title=Ngelencer ke Yogyakarta|last=Tengker|first=Vindex|date=2017-05-15|publisher=Gramedia Pustaka Utama|isbn=9786020353425|language=id}}</ref> [[potato]], [[tofu]], [[tomato]], [[tempeh]], [[egg (food)|eggs]], [[Chicken (food)|chicken]], and fish, and is often sprinkled with [[bawang goreng|fried shallots]] or other variations according to the taste preferences of the communities in each region.
